key_insight: Recurrent neural operators can approximate microstructure-dependent homogenized viscoelastic laws, with a sufficient internal-variable dimension growing logarithmically in inverse relative stress error and material contrast.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates aim to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations while generalizing across loading histories and heterogeneous material properties.
method: Use internal variables to approximate loading-history dependence with Markovian dynamics.
Represent microstructure-dependent constitutive responses with neural operators.
Use a spectral memory-kernel representation to prove uniform approximation for periodic Kelvin–Voigt materials in 2D and 3D.
evidence_signal: Viscoelasticity and crystal-plasticity experiments examine internal-variable dimension and sample complexity, while the theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.
watch_item: The approximation guarantees concern periodic Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity; comparable guarantees for nonlinear crystal plasticity are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
